title: Rònat sent to the stag's school
summary: A boy of ten with a talent for losing count past thirty is sent from his father's holding to the stag's school in the holy wood east of Muileann chiar. Aonghas Cam, the old cutter, scores his first tally-stick through the middle and sets him cutting sticks two years before he is trusted near a beast to be counted.

title: Aonghas Cam's failing thread
summary: A fever settles in the old cutter's crooked leg and will not draw out. Through that winter Rònat watches him grope after names and lines of the long teaching-thread and not always find them, and it is by that fireside, and not by any beast to be counted, that the shape of the sound-marks first comes to him.

title: The first name cut in strokes
summary: Rònat cuts his own name onto a length of ash by a scheme of small strokes, one to a sound, and reads it back cold three days after. He sets the same trick to Aonghas Cam's own name and lays the stick in the old man's hand, who reads his name off it and calls it a count of sounds where he had always cut a count of fish.

title: The death of Aonghas Cam
summary: The old cutter of Muileann chiar's stag school dies in his sleep, having asked that his own years be counted the old way at the last, one stroke to a year, having spent his life trusting a count over a name. Rònat cuts the tally himself.

title: The western teachers come east
summary: Two teachers of the western druid school travel to the far-eastern Muileann chiar to learn Rònat's sound-marks, and stay a season under a man twenty years their junior. Among them is Sìleas nic Ruairidh, eldest of the two, who carries the scheme home and turns it over in her own mind.

title: The letters set against the obelisk
summary: Rònat and two others walk five days west to the grey stone at Cnoc bheag and set the sound-marks stroke for stroke against the old marks cut there. Nothing answers: no vowel, no grouping, no order in the stone's marks matches theirs.

title: The first thing written of the old marks
summary: Before the road home, Rònat cuts onto ash the finding at Cnoc bheag: that the makers of the old stone did not teach the makers of the stag's marks and are not known to them. It is the first thought, rather than a name or a count, that the new marks are made to carry.

title: Niall Òg at the stag's school
summary: The ancient heir passes through the far east on foot and sits two evenings by the school's fire, telling pupils tales of the night of the handful. He asks, at the second evening's end, after the trick of marks he has heard tell of on the road.

title: Niall Òg reads his own name
summary: Rònat cuts Niall Òg's name in the sound-marks and sets the stick in his hand. The old heir, who has been called by his name more times than there are fish in the western sea, reads it back within the hour and laughs until he coughs, saying he has found, at last, a name that stays after the mouth that gave it has gone home.

title: The chest of mismatched tallies opened
summary: Sìleas Dhonn, new in the chair at Dùn dhearg after Dòmhnall Crùbach's death, has brought out and opened before the household the chest she has kept locked for years: her own fair copy of three seasons' Ceann mhin tallies that never matched the toll counted at the gate.

title: Beathan mac Dhonnchaidh's memory found wanting
summary: The old keeper of Muileann shean recites his tally to Sìleas Dhonn from memory, the old way, name for name; she asks him plainly how she is to know it is the same tally he gave the road-guard three seasons past. He has no answer beyond his own honesty, and she sends east for a teacher of the sound-marks.

title: Rònat teaches Sìleas Dhonn's clerks
summary: Rònat walks the last long road of his active years to Dùn dhearg and teaches the ruler's clerks the sound-marks over a winter, finding grown clerks trained to a column of figures quicker with the knife than any pupil he taught in the holy wood.

title: Ailig mac Ruairidh caught by his own gate
summary: The keeper of Ceann mhin's toll, first summoned to render account cut in the new marks and checked against the road-guard's own cutting at his gate, is found short by a sum no honest forgetting explains. It is the first time a keeper's own tally, and not his word, answers for him before the hall.

title: The first whole sentence
summary: Cutting the record of Ailig mac Ruairidh's shortfall for the hall's keeping, Rònat sets down the first whole sentence any hand has yet cut in the sound-marks: that the toll of Ceann mhin was counted short and the keeper answered for it. It stands after him in the hall, saying the same thing to every thumb that reads it.
